headline: Police arrest banned student leader over garment worker clashes in Narayanganj
summary: A case has been filed against 342 people, including 42 named individuals, following clashes between garment workers and police. A banned student leader has been arrested.
details: Police have filed a case against 342 people, including 42 named individuals, following clashes with garment workers in Fatullah, Narayanganj. Most of the named accused are leaders and activists of banned Awami League and its affiliated organizations. Nadim Hossain, the general secretary of the banned Kayetpara Union Chhatra League, has been arrested in connection with the case.

The clashes erupted on Wednesday morning when garment workers, demanding a minimum wage of 30,000 taka, left their factories and occupied the roads in the Katherpool area of Fatullah. They attempted to gather workers from other factories as well.

When police attempted to disperse the workers, a series of chases and clashes ensued. Workers threw bricks, prompting police to use tear gas and sound grenades to disperse the crowd. At least 15 people, including police and workers, were injured, and the glass of several garment factories was broken.

Security has been heightened in the industrial areas and key roads of Narayanganj since Thursday. However, no new labor protests or untoward incidents have been reported. Production activities in garment factories have returned to normal.

Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime) Tarek Al Mehdi stated that Nadim Hossain was arrested from Rupganj. Police have information that Nadim Hossain, through his local contacts, attempted to incite sabotage during the labor movement. His involvement in the Katherpool clashes has been confirmed.

headline_marked: Tk 4,068cr project to [[modernise Mongla Port]] as regional economic hub
headline: Tk 4,068cr project to modernise Mongla Port as regional economic hub
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman laid the foundation stone for the expansion project, aiming to boost trade and industrialisation in the southwest and northwest regions.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman laid the foundation stone for the Tk 4,068 crore Mongla Port Expansion and Modernisation Project in Bagerhat. The project aims to transform the port into a promising economic hub for the southwestern and northwestern regions of Bangladesh.

The modernisation will include the construction of two container jetties, modern container terminals, yards, and cargo-handling facilities. This is seen as a step towards achieving the country's trillion-dollar economic target.
A key feature of the project is the direct rail connectivity between Kamalapur Inland Container Depot in Dhaka and Mongla Port, which will facilitate faster and more efficient cargo transportation.
The Prime Minister emphasized the need for reliable navigation channels, safe vessel movement, and competitive port services to attract international shipping companies.
Beyond the port, the government plans to expand road connectivity from Panchagarh to Mongla and prioritize the development and operation of Khan Jahan Ali Airport.
The project is expected to create sustainable socio-economic value by generating employment for the youth and boosting investor confidence in the region.
Tarique Rahman also called for environment-friendly services, pollution control, and the use of renewable energy to ensure the które which is climate-resilient infrastructure.
The Prime Minister also mentioned that the government has already started working on ensuring gas supplies to industries in the region to revive the industrial heritage of the Khulna region.
